title: arXiv physics — notable papers from the 22 October 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred editorial ranking based on checkable result specificity, experimental or observational basis, cross-list relevance, publication or data/code signals, and independent discussion where found. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old; this is a notable-paper selection, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
sections.abstract: The authors use an optical superlattice to let the coherent superfluid component flow much faster than the normal component, enabling repeated filtering and purification of the superfluid.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report dynamical superfluid-selective transport and repeated normal-component filtering in an ultracold gas, with a flow-rate contrast of 500(49) and oscillations through 100 cycles.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; optical-superlattice ultracold-gas transport with site-resolved population measurements and a microscopic model
sections.unique_caveat: Selectivity relies on slow normal-component thermalization in this low-dimensional lattice setup; equivalent performance in other quantum-fluid platforms or regimes is not established.
sections.ranking_evidence: Direct laboratory demonstration with quantified flow contrast and coherent cycles; cross-listed in three physics subfields.

sections.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
sections.abstract: Using complementary turbulence diagnostics, the authors report evidence that an edge-originating quasi-coherent mode couples to core turbulence and is associated with forward transfer across plasma scales.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret measurements as evidence for net forward energy transfer from ion to electron scales through cross-scale wave-wave interactions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; combined collective Thomson scattering and Doppler backscattering diagnostics in tokamak plasma
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes evidence consistent with the mechanism; its prevalence across discharges and quantitative impact on confinement require further tests.
sections.ranking_evidence: Direct experimental result combining two complementary diagnostics on a fusion-relevant cross-scale transport problem.

sections.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
sections.abstract: Multi-frequency radio maps of ORC4 show spectral structure that the authors interpret as evidence for shock re-acceleration of a pre-existing relativistic-electron population.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find convex spectral curvature and radial flattening that standard thermal-particle shock acceleration and ageing do not explain, and infer likely re-acceleration of a fossil relativistic reservoir.
sections.evidence_type: observational; LOFAR, upgraded GMRT, and MeerKAT imaging and spectral-index analysis over 50–1284 MHz, with auxiliary survey images
sections.unique_caveat: Fossil-electron re-acceleration is an interpretation; odd-radio-circle formation remains debated and the spectrum does not uniquely identify the source history.
sections.ranking_evidence: Broad frequency coverage from three radio arrays, measured spectral quantities with uncertainties, referee resubmission noted, and secondary summaries found in web search.

sections.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
sections.abstract: Forward and backward checks using Pantheon+ supernova data find that peculiar-velocity corrections reduce, but do not remove, a discrepancy between two local-distance-ladder rungs under the adopted framework.
sections.claimed_result: With Manticore-Local peculiar-velocity corrections, the authors report significance falling from 6.8σ to 3.9σ in the forward check and from 7.3σ to 4.3σ in the backward check.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova samples with Planck-CMB priors and peculiar-velocity corrections
sections.unique_caveat: The residual depends on flat-ΛCDM, velocity reconstruction, sample selection, and calibration; the authors call for further systematic tests.
sections.ranking_evidence: Two-direction consistency analysis quantifies the effect of a local-velocity reconstruction on an active cosmological inference problem.

sections.title: Magnetic Activity as a Driver of Low-gravity-like Spectral Morphology in Late-M Dwarfs
sections.abstract: The authors find activity indicators correlate with low-gravity-like near-infrared spectra in late-M dwarfs and propose that persistent small-scale activity can mimic low surface gravity.
sections.claimed_result: One-component PHOENIX/NewEra fits favor lower-gravity spectra for all targets; activity and X-ray indicators correlate with the morphology, and a simplified radiative-transfer experiment produces similar features at fixed gravity.
sections.evidence_type: observational and computational; JWST NIRISS/SOSS, IRTF/SpeX, flare/X-ray measurements, spectral modeling, and radiative-transfer experiment
sections.unique_caveat: The microflare explanation is not directly established by the two TRAPPIST-1 flare time series; primary spectral fits use a one-component atmosphere model.
sections.ranking_evidence: Combines TRAPPIST-1/JWST with 22 late-M dwarfs and multiple activity indicators, reports significant correlations, and received secondary astronomy-news coverage.

sections.title: A 13 Year Black Hole Microlensing Survey in Omega Centauri
sections.abstract: A search of 13 years of Hubble imaging finds no convincing stellar-mass black-hole microlensing events in Omega Centauri; the authors release the photometric dataset.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no convincing candidates and, from completeness and simulation analysis, expect no events in this dataset, contrary to earlier expectations.
sections.evidence_type: observational and computational; Hubble imaging, synthetic microlensing events, Omega Centauri Monte Carlo simulation, and neural-network classification
sections.unique_caveat: The nondetection does not establish an absence of stellar-mass black holes; interpretation depends on the assumed population simulation and survey completeness.
sections.ranking_evidence: Nearly 200 Hubble images spanning 13 years, validated completeness analysis, and a released photometric dataset; submitted to MNRAS.

sections.title: A Generalized Framework for Rapid Polarization Response Generation in Wide Field-of-View Compton Polarimeters
sections.abstract: The authors construct full off-axis polarization responses for planar Compton polarimeters using at least 95% fewer Monte Carlo simulations than the conventional approach.
sections.claimed_result: The second mode reproduces simulated azimuthal distributions to statistical noise and recovers tested polarization measurements using two polarized simulations per energy plus an unpolarized one.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerical response model validated against GEANT4 simulations, with POLAR as a case study
sections.unique_caveat: The faster first mode underestimates polarization for the brightest GRBs; validation is against GEANT4 and tested POLAR cases, not universal instrument calibration.
sections.ranking_evidence: Accepted for ApJ, open-source software, GEANT4 validation, cross-listing in instrument and high-energy astrophysics; DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/aeb548.

sections.title: Sound-Horizon-Agnostic Forecast for Constraints on H0 and Σmν from BAO, CMB Lensing, Supernovae and LSST-like Galaxy Lensing
sections.abstract: The authors forecast joint Hubble-constant and neutrino-mass constraints from BAO, CMB lensing, supernovae, and LSST-like lensing while treating the baryon-drag sound horizon as free.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed neutrino mass, the forecast gives σ(H0)≈1.5 km/s/Mpc under the least informative prior set; with variable neutrino mass it forecasts a 95% upper limit near 0.4 eV and weaker H0 constraints.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; LSST-like galaxy lensing and Simons-Observatory-like CMB lensing combined with DESI BAO and expanded supernova samples
sections.unique_caveat: Forecasts are not observations; mock tests recover unbiased H0 for modified recombination but not early dark energy, showing dependence on early-Universe assumptions.
sections.ranking_evidence: Combines complementary cosmological probes, marginalizes over lensing systematics, and validates the method against mocks; included as a test strategy, not a new measurement.
